pharm-heme:coagmap.q: Which drug inhibits the P2Y12 ADP receptor?
pharm-heme:coagmap.e: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits COX; abciximab blocks GP IIb/IIIa.
Indirect Xa inhibitor; no protamine reversal.

pharm-heme:coagmap.q: A 55-year-old man takes low-dose aspirin after a myocardial infarction. Before elective surgery he is told to stop it 7 days in advance because its antiplatelet effect persists for the life of the platelet. Which action explains this?
pharm-heme:coagmap.e: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates COX-1, and anucleate platelets cannot make new enzyme, so ↓ TXA₂ lasts 7–10 days; P2Y12 blockade is the clopidogrel class.

pharm-heme:heparin.e: Antithrombin then inactivates thrombin (IIa) and Xa. Monitor aPTT for unfractionated heparin.
Protamine is positively charged and binds heparin.

pharm-heme:heparin.q: A 66-year-old woman with an acute pulmonary embolism and stable BP is started on an IV anticoagulant infusion titrated to the aPTT. The drug has no anticoagulant effect unless it binds which plasma protein?
pharm-heme:heparin.e: Unfractionated heparin binds antithrombin and accelerates its inactivation of thrombin and factor Xa; protein C is a vitamin K–dependent anticoagulant unrelated to heparin.

pharm-heme:warfarin.e: ↓ γ-carboxylation of II, VII, IX, X, protein C and S.

o: Safe in the first trimester only
pharm-heme:warfarin.e: Crosses the placenta; heparin/LMWH is used in pregnancy.

pharm-heme:warfarin.q: A 45-year-old woman on warfarin for atrial fibrillation has had a stable INR of 2.5. She starts a 4-drug regimen for pulmonary tuberculosis, and 3 weeks later her INR is 1.3. What best explains the change?
o: ↓ Vitamin K absorption from the gut
pharm-heme:warfarin.e: Rifampin induces CYP2C9/3A4, accelerating warfarin clearance and lowering the INR; enzyme inhibitors would raise it.

pharm-heme:hepvswar.q: Which anticoagulant has rapid onset and works in vitro and in vivo?
pharm-heme:hepvswar.e: Warfarin works only in vivo and takes days.

pharm-heme:hepvswar.q: Which is metabolized by CYP2C9 and has many drug interactions?
A 29-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation has a swollen, painful left leg, and compression ultrasound confirms a proximal DVT. Which anticoagulant is preferred?
pharm-heme:hepvswar.e: LMWH does not cross the placenta and is preferred in pregnancy; warfarin is teratogenic and DOACs are not recommended.

pharm-heme:doac.e: Oral; no routine monitoring; reversed by andexanet alfa.
Dabigatran is an oral direct thrombin inhibitor.

pharm-heme:doac.q: A 68-year-old woman with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation wants an oral anticoagulant that does not need INR monitoring and is started on apixaban. How does this drug prevent clot formation?
pharm-heme:doac.e: Apixaban and rivaroxaban bind factor Xa directly without antithrombin; dabigatran is the oral direct thrombin inhibitor.

pharm-heme:antiplt.q: Clopidogrel is a prodrug activated by:

pharm-heme:antiplt.e: Block the final common pathway of aggregation.

pharm-heme:antiplt.q: A 58-year-old man receives a coronary stent and is discharged on aspirin and clopidogrel. Four weeks later he has stent thrombosis despite full adherence, and genotyping shows two loss-of-function alleles. What is the most likely reason for treatment failure?
o: Rapid CYP3A4 clearance of active drug
Poor CYP2C19 activation of the prodrug
pharm-heme:antiplt.e: Clopidogrel is a prodrug that needs CYP2C19 for activation; poor metabolizers get little P2Y12 blockade and may switch to ticagrelor or prasugrel.

pharm-heme:lytic.e: Used in early ischemic stroke, STEMI and massive PE.

pharm-heme:lytic.q: A 67-year-old man presents 2 hours after sudden right hemiparesis and aphasia. Noncontrast CT shows no hemorrhage, and BP is 160/90 mm Hg. Which drug and mechanism are most appropriate now?
pharm-heme:lytic.e: IV alteplase within 4.5 h of ischemic stroke onset lyses the clot; aminocaproic acid is an antifibrinolytic that would oppose this.

pharm-heme:cycle.q: Which drug class is S-phase specific?
pharm-heme:cycle.e: Vinca alkaloids and taxanes act in M phase; bleomycin in G₂.
Alkylators and anthracyclines act across phases.

pharm-heme:cycle.q: A 9-year-old boy with acute lymphoblastic leukemia receives vincristine during induction chemotherapy. In which phase of the cell cycle does this drug act?
pharm-heme:cycle.e: Vinca alkaloids block tubulin polymerization and halt mitosis in M phase; antimetabolites act in S phase.

pharm-heme:antibiotic.e: Free-radical DNA strand breaks; minimal myelosuppression.

pharm-heme:antibiotic.q: A 52-year-old woman completed doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide and paclitaxel for breast cancer 1 year ago. She now has exertional dyspnea and ankle edema, and echocardiography shows a dilated left ventricle with EF 30%. Which mechanism most likely caused her heart failure?
o: Inhibition of HER2 signaling in myocytes
pharm-heme:antibiotic.e: Anthracyclines cause dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy through iron-dependent free radicals (dexrazoxane protects); acrolein from cyclophosphamide injures the bladder.

pharm-heme:antimet.e: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, which inactivates 6-MP. Reduce 6-MP or azathioprine dose with allopurinol; TPMT deficiency also ↑ toxicity.

pharm-heme:antimet.q: A 45-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on weekly methotrexate develops mouth ulcers and fatigue. Hb is 9.2 g/dL with MCV 110 fL and hypersegmented neutrophils. Which laboratory pattern is expected?
pharm-heme:antimet.e: Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, producing functional folate deficiency (↑ homocysteine only); B₁₂ deficiency also raises methylmalonic acid.

pharm-heme:alkyl.q: Cyclophosphamide causes hemorrhagic cystitis prevented by:

pharm-heme:alkyl.e: Prevent with amifostine and chloride diuresis.

pharm-heme:alkyl.q: A 40-year-old woman receiving IV cyclophosphamide for lupus nephritis develops painful gross hematuria. Urinalysis shows red cells without casts, and cystoscopy shows diffuse bladder mucosal hemorrhage. Which metabolite is responsible?
pharm-heme:alkyl.e: Acrolein injures the urothelium and is neutralized by mesna; phosphoramide mustard is the active DNA-alkylating metabolite.

pharm-heme:mitosis.e: Taxanes prevent breakdown and hyperstabilize polymerized microtubules in M phase.

pharm-heme:mitosis.q: A 6-year-old girl undergoing induction therapy for acute lymphoblastic leukemia develops severe constipation, jaw pain, bilateral foot drop and absent ankle reflexes. What is the mechanism of the drug most likely responsible?
pharm-heme:mitosis.e: Vincristine binds tubulin and prevents microtubule assembly, causing neuropathy including autonomic constipation; taxanes instead stabilize microtubules.

pharm-heme:tamox.e: Agonist at endometrium and bone; antagonist at breast.

pharm-heme:tamox.q: A 46-year-old premenopausal woman takes tamoxifen after surgery for ER-positive breast cancer. She develops depression, and her oncologist advises against paroxetine because it may reduce tamoxifen's efficacy. Paroxetine would do this by inhibiting which enzyme?
pharm-heme:tamox.e: Tamoxifen is a prodrug activated by CYP2D6 to endoxifen, its most potent antiestrogenic metabolite; strong CYP2D6 inhibitors such as paroxetine and fluoxetine lower endoxifen levels. Weak CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., venlafaxine, citalopram) are preferred.

pharm-heme:mabs.q: A 50-year-old woman with HER2-positive breast cancer receiving trastuzumab develops exertional dyspnea, and her LVEF has fallen from 62% to 40%. Which feature characterizes this cardiotoxicity?
pharm-heme:mabs.e: Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity is not dose-related and usually recovers after the drug is held; dose-dependent irreversible free-radical injury is anthracycline toxicity.

pharm-heme:smi.q: A 48-year-old man has fatigue, early satiety and splenomegaly. WBC is 120,000/µL with all stages of granulocyte maturation, and karyotype shows t(9;22). What is the mechanism of the first-line drug?
pharm-heme:smi.e: Chronic myeloid leukemia is driven by the BCR-ABL fusion kinase, which imatinib inhibits; JAK2 inhibitors target polycythemia vera and myelofibrosis.

pharm-heme:ameliorate.q: Leucovorin is given with methotrexate to:
o: Rescue normal cells by bypassing DHFR

pharm-heme:ameliorate.e: Aprepitant (NK₁) and dexamethasone are added for highly emetogenic regimens.

pharm-heme:ameliorate.q: A 55-year-old man receiving cisplatin for head and neck cancer has persistent vomiting on days 2–4 despite ondansetron and dexamethasone. Adding aprepitant helps by which mechanism?
pharm-heme:ameliorate.e: Delayed chemotherapy-induced emesis is mediated by substance P at NK₁ receptors, which aprepitant blocks; ondansetron already provides 5-HT₃ blockade.

pharm-heme:keytox.q: Ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity are typical of:

A 32-year-old man treated with ABVD chemotherapy for Hodgkin lymphoma 6 months ago has progressive dyspnea and dry cough. There are bibasilar crackles, and pulmonary function tests show a restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO. Which drug is most likely responsible?
pharm-heme:keytox.e: Bleomycin causes dose-related pulmonary fibrosis; doxorubicin in the same regimen causes cardiomyopathy instead.

pharm-heme:hematinic.e: Bone pain is common; used for chemotherapy neutropenia.

pharm-heme:hematinic.q: A 60-year-old man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease has fatigue and Hb 8.5 g/dL with a normocytic anemia. Ferritin and transferrin saturation are normal. He is started on the missing renal hormone. Which adverse effect is most likely?
pharm-heme:hematinic.e: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents raise BP and thrombotic risk, especially when Hb is pushed above 11–12 g/dL; they do not cause hypotension.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ขาบวมหลังผ่าตัด
title.en: Boss case: Swollen leg after surgery

boss.case: A 58-year-old woman, 6 days after hip replacement, has a swollen, tender left calf. She has received unfractionated heparin since surgery. Platelets fell from 260,000 to 95,000/µL. Doppler confirms a new DVT.

qs.q: The most likely cause of the platelet fall:
qs.e: Antibodies to heparin–PF4 complexes activate platelets 5–10 days after exposure → thrombosis.
Stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. LMWH cross-reacts; warfarin alone can cause venous limb gangrene.
Hepatically cleared; bivalirudin is another DTI.
Warfarin affects the extrinsic pathway factor VII first.

qs.q: Why is warfarin overlapped with a parenteral anticoagulant at start?
o: Heparin blocks warfarin metabolism by CYP2C9
Protein C falls first → transient hypercoagulability
The overlap lowers the risk of major bleeding
qs.e: Protein C has a short half-life; risk of warfarin skin necrosis.

qs.q: Bleeding on warfarin with high INR is reversed rapidly by:
qs.e: Protamine reverses heparin; idarucizumab reverses dabigatran.

stem.th: ชาย 50 ปี อ่อนเพลีย อิ่มเร็ว ม้ามโตคลำได้ใต้ชายโครง 8 cm
stem.en: A 50-year-old man has fatigue and early satiety; spleen is palpable 8 cm below the costal margin.

steps.q: To prevent tumor lysis with cytoreduction, give:
steps.e: Allopurinol ↓ urate formation; rasburicase (urate oxidase) breaks it down. Uricosurics raise the risk of urate nephropathy.
